newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Events leading to local council polls in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Events leading to local council polls in Nigeria.

text.p: Nigerians voted peacefully on Saturday in municipal polls considered a test of the ruling military's commitment to hand power over to civilian leaders next year.
These were the first polls contested on party lines since then military rulers scrapped civilian-rule presidential elections in June 1993 as wealthy businessman Moshood Abiola headed for victory.
Here are key events leading to the latest election:
-- November 17, 1993 - General Sani Abacha, defence minister in an interim government, seizes power amid political crisis and violence following annulment of presidential poll.

-- June 1994 - Abiola proclaims himself president, is arrested and charged with treason. Riots and strikes erupt. The military government inaugurates constitutional conference to write a new charter to lead Nigeria to democratic rule.
-- August 1994 - Many labour leaders and Abiola lieutenants are arrested in crackdown on strikes; Opposition figures such as Nobel Literature laureate Wole Soyinka flee abroad.
-- October 1995 - Abacha unveils transition to democracy programme to hand over to an elected president in three years.

-- November 1995 - Writer Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight members of his Movement for the Survival of Ogoni Peoples are hanged for murder of four Ogoni chiefs in a trial condemned internationally as flawed. Commonwealth suspends Nigeria. United States, European Union and South Africa impose arms and visa restrictions and call for quicker restoration of democracy but Nigeria says it will stick with its own transition plan.
-- January 1996 - Abacha's eldest son is killed in a plane crash in which a shadowy group claims responsibility. Bombs explode in the north killing one person.
-- June 1996 - Abiola's senior wife Kudirat is killed by unknown gunmen who shoot her in her car along a Lagos road.
-- September 1996 - Five political parties are registered to contest for power in civilian-rule elections.
-- December 1996 - Bombs linked to the political crisis blast army bus, killing a soldier and and wounding dozens of others.
